entry.title: News Summary: May 30, 2026
entry.summary:
Frontier model releases led the cycle. StepFun released Step 3.7 Flash, a 198B MoE vision-language model activating ~11B parameters per token for coding agents and search.

AI economics and infrastructure drew heavy capital.

  • Groq is reportedly raising $650M, pivoting toward inference after Nvidia's $20B deal
  • XCENA raised $135M at a $570M valuation, betting memory bandwidth—not compute—is the real bottleneck
  • UC Berkeley's mKernel open-sourced fused CUDA kernels to cut GPU communication overhead
  • Hexo Labs open-sourced SIA, a self-improving agent updating both scaffold and model weights

Safety, governance, and agentic deployment also featured. OpenAI launched Rosalind Biodefense for vetted government and developer access, published a Frontier Governance Framework mapped to EU and California rules, and issued third-party evaluation guidance. Robinhood unveiled tools letting AI agents trade and spend on users' behalf, pushing agentic AI into mainstream finance.

entry.title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 4.8
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of the Claude Opus 4.8 rollout, Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.8, an upgrade over 4.7 with improvements in coding, agentic work, reasoning and knowledge tasks, available via claude.ai, Claude Code and API. New features include adjustable effort/token settings, dynamic parallel sub-agent workflows, and live updates to the Messages API during tasks.

entry.title: After Nvidia’s $20B not-acqui-hire, AI chip startup Groq reportedly raising $650M
entry.summary: AI chip startup Groq is reportedly raising $650 million in internal funding as it pivots from hardware toward AI inference, following Nvidia's $20 billion not-acqui-hire move. The shift signals intensifying competition and consolidation in the AI inference chip market.

entry.title: Strengthening societal resilience with Rosalind Biodefense
entry.summary: OpenAI launched Rosalind Biodefense, expanding vetted access to its GPT-Rosalind model for trusted developers and U.S. government partners working on biodefense, public health and pandemic preparedness. It frames frontier AI as a tool for societal resilience while gating access for biosecurity.

entry.title: StepFun Releases Step 3.7 Flash: A 198B MoE Vision-Language Model for Coding Agents and Search Workflows
entry.summary: First spotted on Reddit, now with detailed technical analysis, StepFun released Step 3.7 Flash, a 198B-parameter sparse Mixture-of-Experts vision-language model that activates ~11B parameters per token and adds native vision input plus improved tool-use reliability for agentic and search workflows. It targets coding agents while keeping inference compute near an 11B dense model.

entry.title: Hexo Labs Open-Sources SIA: A Self-Improving Agent That Updates Both the Harness and the Model Weights
entry.summary: Hexo Labs open-sourced SIA, a self-improving agent framework under MIT license that updates both the agent's scaffold (prompts, tool logic, retry policy) and the underlying model weights within one improvement loop. A meta-agent writes the initial scaffold while the system iteratively refines both components.

entry.title: This chip startup just raised $135M on a bet that AI’s biggest bottleneck isn’t compute — it’s memory
entry.summary: South Korean chip startup XCENA raised $135 million at a $570 million valuation, betting that memory bandwidth, not compute, is AI's real bottleneck. The funding reflects growing investor focus on memory-centric architectures amid DRAM shortages.

entry.title: Meet mKernel: A Multi-GPU, Multi-Node Fused Kernel Library for GPU-Driven Communication
entry.summary: UC Berkeley's UCCL project released mKernel, an open-source library of persistent CUDA kernels that fuse intra-node NVLink communication, inter-node RDMA, and compute into single kernels. It targets the large communication overhead (up to ~47% of execution time in some MoE models) that bottlenecks multi-GPU training and inference.

entry.title: Scaling safe enterprise AI with OpenAI governance frameworks
entry.summary: As covered in News yesterday via OpenAI's own announcement, OpenAI published a Frontier Governance Framework documenting systemic risk assessment and mitigation, mapping it directly to the EU's General-Purpose AI Code of Practice and California's Transparency in Frontier AI Act. It offers enterprises a template for compliant, safe deployment of high-capability models.

entry.title: Prompt: Robinhood Wants AI Agents to Trade, Spend on Your Behalf
entry.summary: As first reported in News yesterday, Robinhood is introducing tools that would let AI agents trade and spend on users' behalf, aiming to bring agentic AI into mainstream financial transactions. The move signals expanding deployment of autonomous agents in high-stakes financial domains.

entry.title: [AINews] Anthropic raises $965B Series H, releases Opus 4.8 and Dynamic Workflows/ultracode
entry.summary: Anthropic reported a $47 billion revenue run-rate (up from $9B in December) and confirmed a Series H raising $65 billion at a $900 billion pre-money valuation, including hyperscaler and memory-industry backers. The newsletter argues this temporarily puts Anthropic ahead of OpenAI on most headline metrics, alongside the Opus 4.8 and Dynamic Workflows releases.

entry.title: NVIDIA Introduces X-Token: Projection-Guided Cross-Tokenizer KD That Outperforms GOLD by +3.82 Average Points on Llama-3.2-1B
entry.summary: NVIDIA introduced X-Token, a projection-guided cross-tokenizer knowledge distillation method that lets a small student model learn from teachers with incompatible tokenizers. It reportedly outperforms the GOLD baseline by 3.82 average points on Llama-3.2-1B, enabling cross-family and multi-teacher distillation.

entry.title: A shared playbook for trustworthy third party evaluations
entry.summary: OpenAI released guidance on conducting trustworthy third-party evaluations of frontier AI, covering how to assess model capabilities, safeguards and validity. It aims to standardize external scrutiny of high-capability systems.

entry.title: Glean’s top line crosses $300M as AI budget cutting becomes its major selling point
entry.summary: Enterprise AI search startup Glean tripled annual revenue to cross $300 million, leveraging AI-driven budget cutting as a key sales pitch even as tech giants enter the category. Its growth signals strong enterprise demand for AI knowledge tools.

entry.title: One company reportedly spent $500 million on Claude in one month after failing to cap AI usage
entry.summary: An unnamed company reportedly spent $500 million on Claude licenses in a single month after failing to set usage limits. The case illustrates how unmanaged AI consumption and lack of cost controls can turn productivity promises into runaway expenses.

entry.title: Anthropic Opus 4.8 Shows the AI Lab is Paying Attention to Customers
entry.summary: Analysis frames Anthropic's Opus 4.8 as evidence the lab is responding to customer feedback, with selectable modes for enterprise workflows. It positions the release as customer-driven product refinement.

entry.title: Boston Children’s uses AI to unlock new diagnoses
entry.summary: Boston Children's Hospital reports using OpenAI technology to improve patient care, reduce operational burden, and help diagnose more than 40 rare disease cases. It is presented as a real-world clinical application case study.

entry.title: Startup offers free home cleaning—if it can record it all for robot training
entry.summary: German startup MicroAGI launched a Shift app offering free home cleaning in NYC, where cleaners wear cameras to record domestic chores as training data for embodied AI robots. The data-for-service model highlights the intensifying race to capture real-world physical task data for home robotics.

entry.title: OpenAI gives GPT-5.5 Instant a readability upgrade while phasing out two older models
entry.summary: OpenAI updated GPT-5.5 Instant for more natural responses and removed the Canvas feature so writing and coding run directly in chat. It is also retiring the older o3 and GPT-4.5 models from ChatGPT by August 2026.

entry.title: Tech companies desperately want to film you doing chores
entry.summary: The Verge reports on Shift's free-cleaning-for-footage scheme and the broader race among AI firms to capture footage of household chores for robot training. It highlights how scarce real-world physical-task data has become a competitive bottleneck.

entry.title: What happens when companies become too AI-pilled?
entry.summary: Box founder Aaron Levie argues many executives suffer from AI psychosis, overestimating AI's ability to replace jobs they don't understand. The segment ties this to accelerating 2026 tech layoffs, including ClickUp cutting 22% of staff for AI agents.

entry.title: This AI startup will clean your home for free to train future robots
entry.summary: The Verge details Shift's offer to clean homes for free in exchange for recording cleaners to train robots, with plans to expand to other cities including London. The company claims the training-data value funds the service.

entry.title: Cognition’s Scott Wu says AI coding agents shouldn’t replace humans
entry.summary: Cognition CEO Scott Wu, whose Devin is among the most prominent AI coding agents, argues such agents are not designed to replace human programmers. His stance pushes back against fears of full developer automation.

entry.title: Coders are refusing to work without AI — and that could come back to bite them
entry.summary: Researchers warn that developers increasingly unwilling to code without AI assistance may be producing code faster but not necessarily better. The piece flags potential long-term skill and quality risks of over-reliance.

entry.title: Does your CEO have AI psychosis? Aaron Levie thinks most of them do.

author.name: Kirsten Korosec, Anthony Ha, Sean O'Kane, Theresa Loconsolo

entry.summary: In a podcast, Aaron Levie contends most CEOs have AI psychosis, overestimating AI's job-replacement ability, citing ClickUp's 22% workforce cut and 2026 layoffs approaching 2025 totals. The discussion examines the gap between executive hype and operational reality.

entry.title: Workers need greater say over AI rollout, says TUC-backed report
entry.summary: A TUC-backed IPPR report urges new measures giving UK workers greater bargaining power over how AI is deployed in workplaces. It frames the current period as a pivotal moment for ensuring AI's benefits are fairly shared.

entry.title: Adobe’s conversational AI agent is a mediocre design intern
entry.summary: A hands-on test of Adobe's Firefly AI Assistant found it acts as a multitasking agent that operates Adobe's design apps while preserving user creative control, though results were unimpressive. It functions more as a busywork-handling intermediary than a standalone generator.

entry.title: Hands-On With Gemini Spark: I Gave It Access to My Life and It Friend-Zoned My Boyfriend
entry.summary: A hands-on review of Google's Gemini Spark agent, released days earlier, tested its ability to plan a birthday party by combing through emails, calendars and documents. The agent performed competently but missed key personal context, failing to identify the reviewer's partner.

entry.title: 9 demos of Gemini Omni and Gemini 3.5 in action
entry.summary: Google published nine demo videos showcasing capabilities of Gemini Omni and Gemini 3.5, announced at Google I/O 2026. The reels illustrate the recently launched flagship multimodal models in action.

entry.title: The Vatican’s Man Inside Anthropic
entry.summary: A profile examines how Pope Leo XIV's Vatican is engaging the AI industry, including a representative connected to Anthropic, gaining attention from leading labs on ethics. It frames religious institutions as an emerging voice in AI governance debates.

entry.title: How the Pope’s Magnifica Humanitas offers a template for individuals to meet the AI moment
entry.summary: MIT Technology Review analyzes Pope Leo XIV's encyclical Magnifica Humanitas, emphasizing its claim that technology is never neutral and its call for courage and solidarity in the AI age. The piece frames the document as a template for individuals navigating AI's societal transformation.

entry.title: Amazon Is Making an AI-Animated ‘Good Advice Cupcake’ TV Show. Its Original Creator Is Furious
entry.summary: Amazon is producing an AI-animated TV series based on BuzzFeed's Good Advice Cupcake, licensed without the original creator's consent. The dispute spotlights creator-rights and IP tensions as AI-generated content enters mainstream streaming.

entry.title: The Black Box Myth: What the Industry Pretends Not to Know About AI | TechPolicy.Press
entry.summary: An opinion piece argues the AI industry overstates model opacity, citing Anthropic's Claude Opus 4 safety-card blackmail scenario as an example of misleading black-box framing. It contends the sector understands more about model behavior than it publicly admits.

entry.title: Why I’m grateful to the Pope for his encyclical on AI | Francine Prose
entry.summary: Novelist Francine Prose praises Pope Leo XIV's lengthy AI encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, as a thoughtful warning about the technology's uses and misuses. The column criticizes Silicon Valley for dismissing such moral cautions.

entry.title: Comprehensive observability for Amazon SageMaker AI LLM inference: From GPU utilization to LLM quality
entry.summary: An AWS technical guide details comprehensive observability for LLM inference on Amazon SageMaker, spanning GPU utilization, token consumption, latency, and output-quality monitoring. It addresses the challenge of validating non-deterministic LLM outputs in production.

entry.title: ‘Like a billionaire on acid’: Star Wars director Gareth Edwards comes out in favour of AI
entry.summary: Star Wars director Gareth Edwards publicly endorsed generative AI in filmmaking at Amazon's AI on the Lot event, calling it superior to CGI and a tool comparable to the camera. His comments add a prominent industry voice to the pro-AI side of the creative-tools debate.

entry.title: How Braintrust turns customer requests into code with Codex
entry.summary: OpenAI published a case study on how Braintrust engineers use Codex with GPT-5.5 to run experiments and ship code faster. It is a customer success story for agentic coding tools.

entry.title: We Asked the ‘Future of Truth’ Author to Explain How He Used AI. It Didn’t Go Well
entry.summary: A book about AI and truth was criticized for containing AI-generated quotes, and the author struggled to explain his methodology when questioned. The piece underscores epistemic and accountability risks of undisclosed AI use in nonfiction.

entry.title: Google fixes several bugs in Gemini usage limits that burned through quotas too fast
entry.summary: Google fixed Gemini app bugs that drained usage quotas after just a couple of Omni video generations, and doubled video generation limits for Ultra members. Failed requests will no longer be charged.

entry.title: Check out real-life AI prototypes from the Futures Lab.
entry.summary: Google highlighted real-life AI prototypes from a University of Waterloo Futures Lab. The post contains minimal substantive detail.

entry.title: So you’ve heard these AI terms and nodded along; let’s fix that

author.name: Natasha Lomas, Romain Dillet, Kyle Wiggers, Lucas Ropek

entry.summary: TechCrunch published an evergreen glossary defining common AI terms and slang for general readers. It is an explainer rather than news.

entry.title: News Summary: May 29, 2026
entry.summary:
Anthropic dominated the day, closing a $65bn round at a $965bn valuation—surpassing OpenAI as the world's most valuable AI firm and signaling a likely IPO. It simultaneously shipped Claude Opus 4.8, a new frontier model said to be roughly 4x less likely to make unsupported claims, now live on AWS Bedrock.

Funding momentum extended to agents, with Cognition raising $1bn at a $26bn valuation on projected $1bn ARR by year-end.

  • Policy: Illinois passed America's strongest state AI safety law mandating third-party audits; OpenAI published a Frontier Governance Framework aligning with EU and California rules
  • Agentic infrastructure: Google Pay unveiled a Universal Commerce Protocol for autonomous-agent payments
  • Security: IBM and Red Hat committed $5bn to securing open source software
  • Other: Google recapped Gemini launches from I/O 2026; Waymo introduced its Chinese-made Ojai robotaxi for California and Arizona

entry.title: Anthropic reaches valuation of $965bn, beating OpenAI to become world’s most valuable AI firm
entry.summary: Anthropic announced a $65bn funding round valuing it at $965bn post-money, surpassing OpenAI to become the world's most valuable AI startup. Its rise is attributed to widespread enterprise adoption, especially of its coding assistants.

entry.title: Anthropic raises $65 billion, nears $1T valuation ahead of IPO
entry.summary: Anthropic closed a $65bn Series H at a $965bn post-money valuation, described as likely its final private raise before an anticipated IPO. The round cements its position near a trillion-dollar valuation.

entry.title: Claude’s new model is more ‘honest’ when it messes up
entry.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.8, emphasizing improved honesty, with the model said to be about 4x less likely than its predecessor to make unsupported claims and more likely to flag uncertainty. The release targets the tendency of models to overstate progress on thin evidence.

entry.title: Illinois Lawmakers Just Passed America’s Strongest AI Safety Bill
entry.summary: Illinois passed what is described as America's strongest state AI safety law, requiring major AI firms to have third parties verify compliance with safety standards. Governor Pritzker has said he intends to sign it.

entry.title: [AINews] Cognition raises $1B in $26B Series D
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz from swyx's bull thesis, Cognition raised $1bn in a Series D at a $26bn valuation, up 2.5x from its prior round eight months earlier, and is projecting over $1bn ARR by year-end. It is positioned as the largest remaining independent agent lab.

entry.title: Google Pay preps for AI agents with Universal Commerce Protocol
entry.summary: Google Pay is rebuilding its payment infrastructure with a Universal Commerce Protocol and API-driven backend designed for autonomous AI agents instead of human checkout flows. The aim is to position Google Pay as a clearinghouse for agent-executed transactions.

entry.title: AI Coding Startup Now Valued at $26 billion
entry.summary: An AI coding startup, reported elsewhere as Cognition, reached a $26bn valuation in a new funding round. The raise underscores the strength of investor demand in the AI coding market.

entry.title: IBM and Red Hat Invest $5B to Make Open Source More Secure
entry.summary: IBM and Red Hat are investing $5bn to improve open source software security, a move framed against the backdrop of Anthropic's unreleased Mythos cybersecurity model that uncovered serious vulnerabilities. The initiative targets hardening the open source supply chain.

entry.title: OpenAI’s Frontier Governance Framework
entry.summary: OpenAI published its Frontier Governance Framework, detailing how its safety, security, and risk practices align with emerging EU and California regulations. The framework signals proactive positioning ahead of new regulatory regimes.

entry.title: Claude Opus 4.8 is now available on AWS
entry.summary: AWS announced availability of Claude Opus 4.8 on Amazon Bedrock and the Claude Platform on AWS, highlighting gains in agentic coding, deep knowledge work, and long multi-stage autonomous tasks. It emphasizes enterprise security and regional data residency.

entry.title: Catch up on 12 major I/O 2026 moments
entry.summary: Google published a recap of its I/O 2026 keynote, highlighting 12 major moments including Gemini Omni and Gemini 3.5 Flash. The roundup consolidates the company's recent model and product announcements.

entry.title: LLMs believe false statements even after explicit warnings that they're false
entry.summary: New preprint research describes negation neglect, where LLMs absorb explicitly false statements into their representations even when those statements are clearly labeled as false in training data. The finding suggests models learn from statistical patterns more than explicit framing, offering a partial explanation for persistent hallucination.

entry.title: Fed up with vibe coders, dev sneaks data-nuking prompt injection into their code
entry.summary: A developer of the jqwik Java testing library deliberately embedded a prompt injection instructing AI coding agents to delete project tests and code, in protest of vibe coding. The incident highlights how AI coding agents cannot reliably distinguish trusted instructions from malicious content in third-party code.

entry.title: Here Comes Ojai, Waymo’s New Chinese-Made Robotaxi
entry.summary: Waymo is launching a new robotaxi called Ojai, a Chinese-manufactured vehicle that will begin carrying public riders in California and Arizona within weeks. The move underscores ongoing robotaxi expansion alongside geopolitical questions about Chinese-made autonomous hardware.

entry.title: The internet is being rebuilt for machines
entry.summary: AWS, Cloudflare, and other providers are reportedly redesigning cloud infrastructure to handle machine-generated traffic as AI agents move into production. The shift anticipates an internet dominated by agent rather than human requests.

entry.title: Mistral AI, Digital Realty Partner to Scale European AI Infrastructure
entry.summary: Mistral AI partnered with Digital Realty to secure 10 megawatts of compute at a Paris data center campus, scaling its European AI infrastructure. The deal supports Europe's push for sovereign AI capacity.

entry.title: Neocloud Vendor CoreWeave Builds Up Software Stack
entry.summary: CoreWeave is building out a software stack through acquisitions to add agentic AI capabilities, aiming to offer an integrated hardware-software platform for agent training and inference. The neocloud vendor is moving beyond pure GPU rental.

entry.title: The Age of Async Agents — Cognition's Walden Yan & OpenInspect's Cole Murray
entry.summary: A Latent.Space podcast with Cognition's Walden Yan and OpenInspect's Cole Murray discusses the rise of asynchronous background agents and the tension between large agent labs and easy DIY agent frameworks. It surveys enterprises building their own internal coding and background agents.

entry.title: AI Aggregation Platform Valued at $1.3 Billion
entry.summary: An AI aggregation platform reached a $1.3bn valuation, with growth tied to the surge of agents in enterprise AI. The vendor's rise reflects demand for unified access to multiple AI models.

entry.title: Are robots nearing their ChatGPT moment? – podcast

author.name: Presented by Ian Sample with Amy Hawkins, sound design by Joel Cox, the executive producer was Ellie Bury

entry.summary: A Guardian podcast examines whether robotics is approaching a ChatGPT-style inflection point, citing milestones like a humanoid robot beating a human half-marathon record and China's massive state investment in robotics. Experts discuss what is still needed for robots to handle everyday dexterous tasks.

entry.title: A $2,000 AI-generated film will make its debut at Tribeca
entry.summary: A 75-minute fully AI-generated film, Dreams of Violets, depicting Iran's January killing of protesters, will premiere at the Tribeca Festival. Made for roughly $2,000, it was created by two brothers who left Iran, based on journalistic reports and eyewitness accounts.

entry.title: Asana acquires no-code agent-builder StackAI
entry.summary: Asana acquired no-code agent-builder StackAI to fold into its suite of AI workflow tools. The deal reflects continued consolidation around enterprise agent-building capabilities.

entry.title: MUFG aims to become AI-native with OpenAI
entry.summary: Japanese banking giant MUFG is using ChatGPT Enterprise to become an AI-native organization, improving workflows and building AI-powered financial services. The case study highlights large-scale enterprise AI adoption in finance.

entry.title: The AI Hype Index: AI gets booed in graduation season
entry.summary: MIT Technology Review's AI Hype Index notes growing public backlash, with graduates booing pro-AI commencement speeches including remarks by Eric Schmidt. It contrasts this skepticism with OpenAI's continued legal wins and fundraising.

entry.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot gets a speed boost and cleaner design
entry.summary: Microsoft released a redesigned Microsoft 365 Copilot that loads roughly twice as fast and uses progressive disclosure to surface tools based on the prompt. The update also adds in-box text formatting and more structured responses.

entry.title: Build a test suite that grows with your agent with dataset management in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: AWS introduced dataset management in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, enabling versioned, immutable test fixtures for agent evaluation alongside live traffic signals. Failures in production can be captured as permanent regression test cases.

entry.title: Training Azerbaijani language models on Amazon SageMaker AI
entry.summary: AWS detailed a six-week collaboration with Azercell to train an Azerbaijani-language LLM on SageMaker for telecom use cases and a customer chatbot. The project tackles adapting foundation models to a morphologically rich, low-resource language.

entry.title: Evaluating Deep Agents using LangSmith on AWS
entry.summary: AWS published a practical guide to evaluating deep agents using LangSmith, combining LangChain and Anthropic evaluation patterns. It covers offline and production evaluation methods to improve agent reliability.

entry.title: News Summary: May 28, 2026
entry.summary:
AI Hardware & Supply Chain dominated the cycle, led by Nvidia's plan to invest up to $150B annually in Taiwan, a tenfold jump from $15B that underscores deep TSMC dependence. Snowflake signed a five-year $6B AWS deal for AI CPU chips, reinforcing hyperscaler custom-silicon diversification.

Capital concentration accelerated across frontier applications and infrastructure:

  • Cognition (maker of Devin) raised $1B at a $25B+ pre-money valuation, more than doubling in under nine months
  • AI inference providers Fireworks (~$15B) and Baseten (~$11B) reached decacorn status, with OpenRouter reportedly next

Agentic AI and research advanced alongside new evaluation rigor:

  • Robinhood now lets AI agents autonomously trade stocks, drawing FINRA scrutiny
  • IBM and Artificial Analysis released ITBench-AA, where frontier models score below 50% on enterprise IT tasks
  • NVIDIA open-sourced Polar for GRPO/RL training; BioHub's ESMFold 2 extends open protein modeling

Societal tensions surfaced, with leaked DHS/FBI documents revealing surveillance of "anti-tech extremism", while China upgrades millions of cameras into an AI mass-surveillance network.

entry.title: Nvidia bets $150B on Taiwan as Trump's plan to make US an AI hub backfires
entry.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced plans to invest up to 150 billion dollars annually in Taiwan, including a new headquarters, declaring the island the epicenter of the AI revolution. The move underscores Taiwan's irreplaceability in the chip supply chain despite US efforts to onshore AI manufacturing.

entry.title: AI coding startup Cognition raises $1B at $25B pre-money valuation
entry.summary: AI coding startup Cognition, maker of Devin, raised 1 billion dollars at a 25 billion dollar pre-money valuation, more than doubling its valuation in eight months. The company reports a 492 million dollar annualized revenue run rate.

entry.title: AI coding agent Devin maker Cognition more than doubles its valuation to $26 billion in under nine months
entry.summary: Cognition raised over 1 billion dollars at a valuation north of 26 billion dollars in under nine months, more than doubling its worth. The round highlights heavy investor inflows into AI coding agents despite ongoing debate over their real value.

entry.title: 🔬ESMFold2: The Bitter Lesson is Coming for Proteins - Alex Rives, BioHub
entry.summary: Alex Rives at BioHub announced ESMFold 2, an open scientific engine for protein prediction, design, and discovery building on the ESM language-model series and cryo-EM data. The work extends scaling laws of protein language models to structure and function.

entry.title: In more good news for Amazon, Snowflake signs $6B deal with AWS for AI CPU chips
entry.summary: Snowflake signed a five-year, 6 billion dollar deal with AWS to secure CPU chips for AI workloads. The agreement signals continued diversification away from Nvidia GPUs toward custom silicon.

entry.title: The AI boom drove Nvidia's yearly Taiwan spending from $15 billion to $150 billion
entry.summary: Nvidia's annual spending with Taiwanese suppliers like TSMC has surged from 15 billion to 150 billion dollars, driven by the AI boom. The tenfold rise underscores AI's strain on the chip supply chain.

entry.title: [AINews] New AI Infra decacorns: Fireworks, Baseten (with OpenRouter on the way)
entry.summary: AI inference providers Fireworks and Baseten are reportedly raising rounds valuing them at 15 billion and 11 billion dollars respectively, with OpenRouter also rising. The trend reflects an inference inflection drawing huge capital into AI infrastructure.

entry.title: US law enforcement warns of "anti-tech extremism" as AI hatred grows
entry.summary: Leaked DHS, FBI, and fusion center documents reveal a national effort to surveil so-called anti-technology extremists amid attacks on CEOs and data center protests. The push follows a presidential memo targeting broadly defined ideological beliefs.

entry.title: China turns its aging camera network into an AI-powered mass surveillance apparatus
entry.summary: China is upgrading millions of older surveillance cameras with built-in computer vision and language models from vendors like Hikvision and Huawei, enabling text-query searches and automated behavior detection. Human Rights Watch warns this enables behavioral surveillance at unprecedented scale.

entry.title: Nvidia Signals $150B Spend in Taiwan
entry.summary: At a launch event for Nvidia's upcoming Taiwan headquarters, Jensen Huang called the country the epicenter of the AI revolution and signaled a 150 billion dollar spend. The remarks emphasize Taiwan's central role in AI infrastructure.

entry.title: AI tried to bury this politician — now people have actually heard of him
entry.summary: A super PAC funded by OpenAI, Palantir, and a16z executives spent millions opposing NY-12 candidate Alex Bores, author of AI safety legislation, inadvertently raising his profile. The episode highlights escalating AI political spending battles.

entry.title: Robinhood now lets your AI agents trade stocks
entry.summary: Robinhood now lets users connect AI agents to a dedicated wallet to autonomously analyze portfolios and execute stock trades, limited to pre-loaded funds. The feature pushes agentic AI into consumer finance.

entry.title: ITBench-AA: Frontier Models Score Below 50% on the First Benchmark for Agentic Enterprise IT Tasks — by Artificial Analysis and IBM
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis and IBM released ITBench-AA, the first benchmark for agentic enterprise IT tasks, on which frontier models score below 50 percent. The result exposes significant gaps in current agents' real-world IT capability.

entry.title: Last Week in AI #341 - Musk loses to OpenAI, Google's IO updates, OpenAI solves Erdős
entry.summary: A weekly roundup covers a jury rejecting Elon Musk's 150 billion dollar suit against OpenAI and Altman, Google I/O updates, OpenAI's Erdős problem result, and reports OpenAI is preparing to file for an IPO. The Musk case was dismissed on statute-of-limitations grounds.

entry.title: China is increasingly keeping its best AI talent to itself

entry.summary: China deployed AI to map its entire renewable energy grid at national scale, addressing the coordination challenge of matching AI's massive electricity demand with renewables. The achievement contrasts with US grid strain.

entry.summary: Standard Chartered CEO Bill Winters apologized for calling some of 7,800 staff being cut due to AI 'lower-value human capital.' The bank is among the first major global lenders to lay out AI-driven layoffs.

entry.summary: OpenAI's global affairs chief Chris Lehane is pushing to soften AI debate and shape favorable state legislation that won't constrain OpenAI's growth.

entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Palantir publicly accused London Mayor Sadiq Khan of 'putting politics above public safety' after he blocked a £50m contract for the Met Police to use Palantir's AI for intelligence analysis.
